mathematical_reason: The two source-labeled axiomatizations are equivalent: complements follow from X\A, while ordinary countable unions can be made disjoint by replacing A_n with A_n\(⋃_{k<n}A_k). Finite unions needed in that reduction follow from difference/complement closure. The countable-disjoint-union condition must not be read as unrestricted union of arbitrary pairwise-disjoint indexed sets; the indexing is countable. σ-algebra is a family of subsets of a specified X, not automatically the measurable-space pair (X,Σ). This is equivalent to the existing standard complement-and-countable-union formulation by finite Boolean closure and disjointification.
